html:
Added

  • There is always at least one Platform team member (17 Nov 2026): the last platform team member can no longer be deleted, erased or demoted, by any route. The guarantee is in the database: two triggers on users (trg_users_last_platform_team_update_guard and trg_users_last_platform_team_delete_guard, migration 2026_11_17_120000, a metadata change with no rows rewritten) refuse any write that would leave nobody on the team (clearing is_god, clearing super admin by flag or by the role string, setting deleted_at or anonymized_at, deleting the row) with platform_team_last_member. One statement that would remove every member is refused whole. The count of the other members is an ordinary read, not a locking one (a locking read would hold up every new account while a member is being erased), so two different members removed by two different transactions in the same instant are not caught; the Senior accounts page cannot do that, because it locks both rows. status is deliberately not part of the rule (suspending is not deleting or demoting, and a bulk status update must not fail on one row). The requests a person can press ask the same question first (PlatformTeam::isLastMember()) and answer 422 PLATFORM_TEAM_LAST_MEMBER with a message in all eleven languages, before anything is emailed or erased: revoking global super admin in the super admin panel and in a community's admin panel, an admin deleting an account, and a member deleting their own account. GdprService::executeAccountDeletion() stops straight after its lock, before any file or record is removed; an erasure can go ahead once a second member exists. The two admin screens that revoke global super admin (the super admin panel's user list and a community's user edit page) show that refusal from their own wording (admin_super:super.platform_team_last_member, admin_users:user_edit.toasts.platform_team_last_member, eleven languages, the same text as the server's), not the server's raw message, which the admin wording check refuses. Tests: LastPlatformTeamMemberTest (22: every way off the team refused for the only member and allowed when another is left, at the database and at each request); PlatformTeamTest now creates a second member before demoting one, because a fresh test database has no other.
  • Add and remove Platform team members from the Senior accounts page (17 Nov 2026): until now users.is_god could only be set in the database by hand, and nothing recorded it. The Senior accounts page (/platform-team/senior-accounts) now has "Add to the platform team" on a global super admin, "Remove from the platform team" on a member (never on your own row), both ways to put a half-set account right, and "Add someone", which finds any other account by its whole email address (through the existing Find an account request, so the search is recorded and the address is sent in the body) and does both steps (global super admin, then platform team) in one act. Every change asks first. POST /v2/platform-team/senior-accounts/{id}/add-to-team and /remove-from-team (PlatformTeamMembershipService; platform team only, the lock asked before the second sign-in step; a recent second sign-in step; ten changes a minute). The account being added must be active and have two-step sign-in on; a manager's stand-in, a deleted account and an erased one answer 404; nobody can remove themselves, and the caller's and the account's rows are locked together in id order and the caller re-checked, so two members removing each other at once cannot both succeed and the team cannot be left empty. Adding writes flags only, never the role string (F-431); removing clears is_god only, so the account stays a global super admin. Each change is written to super_admin_audit_log in the same transaction under two new action types, platform_team_added and platform_team_removed (migration 2026_11_17_110000, enum members appended with ALGORITHM=INSTANT, LOCK=NONE), plus global_super_admin_granted when the add also set that flag; if the record cannot be written the change is rolled back. The Security page's "Senior access given and removed" lists both, and its note now says only changes made straight in the database go unrecorded. The super admin audit log names both actions. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: PlatformTeamMembershipTest (19: every tier below the platform team refused with nothing changed or recorded; lock before the code; stale second step; each rule; the audit rows; the Security page), SeniorAccountsPage.test.tsx.
  • Push notification records are cleaned up after 180 days (17 Nov 2026): push_log was never pruned. nexus:prune-logs now deletes its rows older than 180 days in every community, a new index on created_at (migration 2026_11_17_100000_add_created_at_index_to_push_log, online, no rows rewritten) keeps that nightly delete from reading the whole table, and the Push notifications page says how long records are kept (kept_days, read from the clean-up's own policy via PruneLogs::retentionDaysFor()). The Clean-up jobs page names push notifications among what "Old log records" deletes.
  • Assurance facts in the Platform team panel (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/assurance ("Assurance facts", last under Access). Seven facts the platform can measure about itself, each as a card with the value in words, when it was read, and a link to the page it comes from: the live version (home page), how many senior accounts have two-step sign-in on (Senior accounts), when the last access review was recorded and whether one is due (Access review), the daily backup check's result (home page; not available with no result in the last 26 hours, the home page's rule), open and overdue requests about personal data across all communities (Data requests), since when failed sign-ins have been counted (Security), and the date of the last independent security test. That date comes only from a new setting, platform_team.last_independent_test_on (env PLATFORM_TEAM_LAST_INDEPENDENT_TEST_ON, YYYY-MM-DD, default none), which the platform's owner sets on the server; unset, malformed or in the future it shows "Not recorded on this server" (a bad value is logged as a warning without the value). The page says first that these are facts to check before quoting them, that open security findings are kept in a private record and not shown, and that an independent test covers the version it tested. It names no customer or community, claims nothing, and has no export, print or copy. GET /v2/platform-team/assurance (platform team only; AssuranceFactsService calls PlatformHealthService::release(), now public, SeniorAccountsService::list(), AccessReviewService::dueStatus(), DataRequestsService::overview() totals and the backup verdict under PlatformHealthService::BACKUP_VERDICT_STALE_SECONDS, now public). 🔴 Each fact is read in its own guard: one that fails is "Could not be read" (logged at error with the fact and the exception class) and the others still answer; never a zero or a tick. Counts, dates and states only. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: AssuranceFactsTest (exact keys and order; each not-available case; three or more sources made to fail alone; the test date rules; no planted name, email, community or id in the body; refused tiers), AssuranceFactsPage.test.tsx (including a check that the English wording has no claim-words).
  • Recent errors: three counts per part of the platform from the error service, switched off until the owner connects it (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/errors ("Recent errors", under Health, after Deployments). When the server has a read-only key for the error service (Sentry), its organisation and the server's project id, it shows for the server, the website and the accessible site (each only when its project id is set) the errors in the last 24 hours, the errors in the last 7 days, and the unresolved problems seen in the last 14 days, with when they were checked. The figures are kept for five minutes; "Check again" asks the error service now (six a minute). A part that could not be read says so, never zero, and an unresolved count the service did not give is "Not available". Until the key is stored the page says "Not connected", what would be needed, and that it is the platform owner's decision, and the server asks the error service nothing. 🔴 Counts only: the server asks for one issue row and reads only the total from the X-Hits header, never a title, message, user, address or tag; the key is never returned, logged or put in an address, and redirects are not followed. New settings in config/services.php (services.sentry.api_token, org, api_base, projects) read SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN_MONITOR, SENTRY_ORG, SENTRY_API_BASE and SENTRY_PROJECT_PHP / _REACT / _WEBUK, listed without values in .env.example. Keys and connections gains a row, "Error service: reading the figures" (sentry_api), set up only when the page above would connect.
  • Addresses and certificates in the Platform team panel (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/domains ("Addresses and certificates", under Health, after Rebuild search). For each community's own main and accessible-site address, and once each for the platform's own addresses (a first section), it says in words whether the address works: "Fine", "Certificate runs out in N days" (21 or fewer), "Not working" with the reason (the name leads nowhere; it leads into a private network so it was not contacted; nothing answered; a browser would not trust the certificate; the certificate could not be read; the certificate has run out), "Not checked yet", or "Not a web address we can check". A community on a platform address is listed as using it. The page says this is what a visitor's browser would be given as seen from the server, so a problem between a visitor and the platform's front door would not show. A new daily command domains:check (05:20, one server, in the background, never overlapping) checks every distinct host once, one after another, and prints one line per host with its status only; a failing host does not fail the command. "Check now" re-checks one community's addresses (or the platform's) in the request. GET /v2/platform-team/domains, POST /v2/platform-team/domains/check with {tenant_id} or {platform: true} (platform team only; 6 a minute; 404 unknown community; who asked is an activity_log row with no community). 🔴 Only hosts read from the tenants table or the platform's own configured list are ever contacted, never one from the request; only a plain host name (no scheme, port, path or IP literal, at most 253 characters); only after OutboundUrlGuard::publicAddressesForHost() approves every address it resolves to, and the connection goes to one of those addresses. The certificate is verified as a browser would (SNI, peer name), with no fallback to an unverified read; 5 second limit. Results are kept per host in the cache for 3 days as a reason code, never an error message or an address. CommunitySetupChecklistService::platformAddresses() and isPlatformAddress() are now public so both pages use one rule. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: DomainCheckTest (a fake prober: no test makes a network connection or DNS lookup; refused tiers probe nothing; a request cannot supply a host; non-public hosts are never connected to; days left at 22, 21, 1, 0 and −1; each reason; no planted error text or address in any response; shared hosts checked once; the schedule), DomainsPage.test.tsx.
  • Agreements and renewals in the Platform team panel (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/agreements ("Agreements and renewals", under Money, after Subscriptions). The platform team keeps the platform's agreements with communities and others: a name and who it is with (both required), and optionally a community, start, renewal and end dates, a contact's name and email, and notes. The list is ordered by the next renewal (no renewal date last, then by name) and says how many days are left; an agreement renewing within 60 days, or whose renewal date has passed, is marked. Ending an agreement keeps it and moves it to an "Ended agreements" list; there is no delete, and the page says so. 🔴 Nothing is filled in that was not typed: an empty field is stored empty and shown as "Not entered". A new home page card agreements is the reminder (needs a look when an agreement that has not ended renews within 60 days or is past its renewal date; no reminder email). GET/POST /v2/platform-team/agreements, PUT /v2/platform-team/agreements/{id}, POST /v2/platform-team/agreements/{id}/end (platform team only: route middleware and a check in each method; 422 with the field and a translated message for each refused value; unknown fields ignored). New table platform_agreements with no community column (migration 2026_11_16_150000, a new table only; community_id is a pointer with no foreign key, so a removed community shows as "Community no longer exists"). Each write is an activity_log row with no community that names the agreement by number only: the contact's name and email never go there. Server messages and page wording in all eleven languages. Tests: PlatformAgreementsTest (every account below the platform team refused on all four requests with nothing written; each rule; the order; days and "renews soon" at 61, 60, 0 and −5 days; the exact fields; the record; the card's four states), PlatformHealthSummaryTest, AgreementsPage.test.tsx, PlatformTeamHome.test.tsx.
  • Rebuild a community's search from the Platform team panel (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/search-rebuild ("Rebuild search", under Health, after Deployments). It lists every community with the last rebuild started from the page ("Never run from this page", "Waiting to start", "Running since …", "Finished …: N entries updated", "Finished with N entries that could not be updated", "Failed") and says whether the search service can be reached. "Rebuild" asks first and says what it does and does not do: it adds and updates the community's search entries; entries for things that were deleted are not removed; members can keep searching while it runs. While any rebuild is waiting or running the list refreshes every 10 seconds. GET/POST /v2/platform-team/search-rebuild (platform team only; POST 6 a minute; 404 unknown community, 409 already waiting or running, 503 search service not answering, nothing queued). The new ReindexTenantSearchJob (queue search, one try, one-hour limit) keeps its state in the cache for 7 days and writes "failed" before any error leaves it; a second delivery of a job that is still running and reporting does not overwrite it. Who started it is an activity_log row with no community. The five "select and index" loops of scripts/sync_search_index.php moved unchanged into the new SearchReindexService (rows sent through a new SearchDocumentIndexer seam so they can be tested without a search server); the script is now a thin caller with the same options, output lines and exit code (output compared before and after on the local database with --dry-run). Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: SyncSearchIndexScriptTest (the script in a child process, written and passing before the move), SearchReindexServiceTest (rows pinned against a verbatim copy of the script's old queries), SearchRebuildTest, SearchRebuildPage.test.tsx.
  • Translations: how much of the wording each language still lacks (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/translations in the Platform team panel, under Keys, after Translation key. Two sections, each with its own "not available" state. "Website wording" reads /translation-coverage.json, written at build time by the new react-frontend/scripts/build-translation-coverage.mjs (run in predev and prebuild after copy-changelog; gitignored) over public/locales; 🔴 the script can never fail a build: on any error it writes {"available": false} and exits 0. "Server wording: emails and messages" reads GET /v2/platform-team/translation-coverage (platform team only), counted over lang/ by TranslationCoverageService and kept for an hour (?refresh=1, the page's "Count again", counts again). For each of the ten languages other than English: phrases, missing (a phrase English has and the language does not, or has empty; plural forms count as one phrase, and any form counts as having it), still the same as English (identical after trimming, and not just a placeholder or a symbol), and the share translated, rounded down so it never shows 100% while anything is left. A server namespace with both a .json and a .php file is counted once per phrase, from the file __() actually reads it from (the .json first, the .php only for phrases the .json lacks). The page says that "same as English" is an upper limit (names and units are meant to stay the same) and that the phone app and the accessible site are not measured. A broken language file counts its phrases as missing; unreadable English is "not available", never zero. nginx.bluegreen.conf gains an exact-match rule so a missing file answers 404, not the app's own page. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: TranslationCoverageTest (fixture lang folder; exact keys; counting; both-files namespace; broken files; kept an hour and recounted on request), scripts/build-translation-coverage.test.mjs (npm run test:translation-coverage), TranslationsPage.test.tsx.
  • Phone app: which versions of the app are in use (16 Nov 2026): the Platform team's Phone app page (/platform-team/phone-app) has a new section, "App versions in use": the phones signed in now, counted by the version of the app they run, newest version first (compared part by part as numbers, so 1.10.0 comes before 1.9.0), and how many signed-in phones have no version recorded. The page says that the figures only cover phones that signed in after this was added, so at first most will show as not recorded. A phone-app sign-in now keeps the app's version on its refresh_session_activity row (new nullable column app_version, migration 2026_11_16_140000), taken from the X-Nexus-Mobile-Version header the app already sends, and only when it is a plain 1.2.3 version (up to three digits per part); anything else, and any sign-in not made through the app, keeps nothing. The version is refreshed by the existing once-a-minute activity write while the app is in use, so an app updated without signing in again is counted under its new version; a request without a valid version leaves it as it was. Nothing new can fail a sign-in or a renewal: the version rides on writes that already happen, and a missing, malformed, over-long or hostile header simply records nothing. GET /v2/platform-team/phone-app (platform team only) gains versions: [{version, sign_ins}] and version_not_recorded: counts only, no member and no device. "Live" is the rule the page already used: a sign-in whose session is neither ended nor expired. Erasing a member already deletes these rows (F-622). Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: PhoneAppVersionRecordTest (stored at sign-in; nine header shapes that sign in normally and store nothing; not from the app; refreshed by later use; left alone by a later bad header), PhoneAppVersionsInUseTest (exact keys; numeric order; only live phone-app sign-ins; nothing recorded yet), PhoneAppPage.test.tsx.
  • Keys and connections: which outside services this server has a key for (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/connections in the Platform team panel, first under Keys. Twenty-six services in twelve groups (email: Gmail API, Postmark, SMTP; live updates: Pusher; phone and browser notifications: Firebase Cloud Messaging, Expo, web push; payments: Stripe and its payment-message key; AI: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini; maps and translation: Google Maps, Google Translate; search: Meilisearch; error reports: Sentry; protection: the Cloudflare origin key, Turnstile, ClamAV; alerts: the two Slack webhooks; sign in with another account: Google, Facebook, Apple; other: Mailchimp, file storage), each shown as "Set up" or "Not set up" with an icon and the words, and a count at the top. Each check reads the same config key the code that uses the service reads, or the same environment value where that code reads the environment directly (Google Maps, Meilisearch, the SMTP host); Gmail counts only with its switch on and all three values; Firebase as FCMPushService decides (the service account file, or the legacy server key). 🔴 GET /v2/platform-team/connections (platform team only) sends key, group and configured per service and nothing else: never a value, a masked value or a length. The page says it never shows a key, that expiry dates are not recorded anywhere, and ends with "Where three other controls are": consent types, the identity check fee (admin Modules page) and the note that the old list of server keys has been replaced by this page. Tests: ConnectionsTest (exact keys; made-up values for six services set, no 4-character piece of any in the response; empty and missing values are not set up; Gmail with the switch off), ConnectionsPage.test.tsx.
  • Deployments: the last deployments and rollbacks this server recorded (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/deployments in the Platform team panel, under Health, after Failed background jobs. Newest first, up to 30: when (in the viewer's own time zone and language), deployment or rollback, succeeded or failed (icon and word), the short version code, the one-line description of the change, how long it took and how many changes it carried. Read from the tail of the deploy record that scripts/deploy/phases/record-deploy-metrics.sh writes (GET /v2/platform-team/deployments, platform team only; only the last 256 KB of the file is read, the file is never loaded whole); an allowlist of fields per line, so the server name and the full and previous commits never leave the server. Where the record does not exist (any machine but the live server) the page says "This server keeps no record of deployments", never "no deployments"; lines that cannot be read are skipped and counted. The page also says that the 30-minute watch after a deployment is not recorded here. New setting platform_team.deploy_history_path (env PLATFORM_TEAM_DEPLOY_HISTORY_PATH) in a new config/platform_team.php.
  • Push notifications: how many notifications reached the push service, by day and by community (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/push-notifications in the Platform team panel, under Communities, after Phone app. For the last 7, 14 or 30 days (14 unless chosen) it shows four figures for every day, quiet days included as zeros: "Accepted by the push service", "Partly accepted", "Failed" and "Nobody to send to" (the member had no phone or browser registered); and for every community the first three over the whole period, with notifications recorded without a community as their own row. The page says at the top that accepted means the push service took it, not that a phone showed it, and that some kinds of notification (event reminders, emergency alerts and some others) are sent without being recorded, so the real numbers are at least these. Days run in the server's time (UTC). Read from push_log (GET /v2/platform-team/push-notifications?days=1..30, platform team only; any other number of days is refused with 422); counts only, never the error text, the title, the kind of notification or who it was for. A record that cannot be read is shown as "Not available", never as zero.
  • Admins are told when a new version of the platform is out (16 Nov 2026): a slim line at the top of the admin panel, under any notice from the platform team: "Version 3.3.0 of the platform is live. See what changed", with a link to the Changelog page. It appears once for each release and stays until the admin closes it; a routine deployment that is not a new release does not bring it back. Which release an admin has closed is remembered in their own browser only, so nothing about who has seen it is kept on the server, and a browser that will not store anything simply shows the line again. It shows nothing at all when the changelog file cannot be read. Admin panel only: not the broker, super admin or Platform team panels. Wording in all eleven languages (admin_nav:whats_new.*). Component react-frontend/src/admin/components/WhatsNewBand.tsx; the version comes from /changelog-data/index.json, the same file the Changelog page reads.
  • Access review: a recorded check of who holds senior access, at least every 90 days (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/access-review in the Platform team panel, under Access, after Find an account. It lists every senior account (the same list as the Senior accounts page, grouped by level) with two choices each, "Keep" and "Should be removed"; nothing is chosen in advance and "Record this review" stays off until every account has a choice. An optional note (up to 500 characters) can be added. Recording needs a recent second sign-in step, asked only after the platform-team check. The server reads the list again and refuses the review ("The list changed while you were reviewing; load it again") unless it covers exactly the current senior accounts, once each. One review row and one line per account are written in one transaction. Recording a review changes nobody's access, and the page says so and where access is actually removed. The page shows when the last review was and who recorded it, whether one is due (none yet, or the newest is more than 90 days old), the accounts marked "Should be removed" last time that still hold their access, and the last ten reviews. A new home page card, Access review, says "Needs a look" when a review is due. Two new platform-wide tables, senior_access_reviews and senior_access_review_items (migration 2026_11_16_120000), hold ids only (no name, no email address) and cannot be changed or deleted afterwards: database triggers refuse it. Endpoints GET and POST /v2/platform-team/access-review, platform team only. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: AccessReviewTest (six refused accounts; lock before second step; exact keys; exact-list refusals write nothing; one row and one line per account; no name or email column; names read live; due at 0, 89 and 91 days; still-open removals; the database refuses changes and deletions), PlatformHealthSummaryTest, AccessReviewPage.test.tsx.
  • Legal documents: which communities have published terms and a privacy notice, and how many members have not accepted them (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/legal-documents in the Platform team panel, under Data and legal, after Data requests. Until now this could only be seen one community at a time. For every community the page lists its terms and its privacy notice (shown as "None" when the community has none) and any other legal document it has (cookie notice, accessibility statement, community guidelines, acceptable use policy), each with whether it is published, which version and since when, whether members are asked to accept it and, when they are, how many of the members asked have not accepted the current version. Members asked means active members who are not administrators, the same people the acceptance prompt asks and the community's own compliance figures count. The communities without a published privacy notice are named at the top. Beside Terms the page says that terms are added automatically when a community is created. "Published" now comes from one shared rule (LegalDocumentPublication) that the Community setup page also uses, so the two pages cannot disagree. Counts only: no member, document title or text, IP address or browser detail leaves the server. A figure the server cannot read says "Not available", never zero. Documents are still written in each community's own admin panel; this page changes nothing. Endpoint GET /v2/platform-team/legal-documents, platform team only. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: LegalDocumentsTest (four accounts; exact keys; planted name, email, IP address, browser and document text are not in the response; every community listed with terms and privacy; other kinds after them; same published rule as Community setup; version and date only when published; who is asked; figures equal to getComplianceSummary() for one community; an unreadable figure is not available; POST, PUT and DELETE change nothing), CommunitySetupTest, LegalDocumentsPage.test.tsx.
  • Clean-up jobs, and the state of the database backup, in the Platform team panel (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/clean-up-jobs, under Data and legal, after Legal documents. It lists the fifteen scheduled jobs that delete data (eight scheduled commands: performance:prune, retention:enforce, nexus:prune-logs, nexus:prune-match-notifications, safeguarding:purge-message-copies, federation:purge-external-logs, federation:prune-aggregate-logs, groups:prune-exports; and seven jobs of the every-minute runner: cleanup, cleanup-sessions, story-cleanup, gdpr-export-cleanup, abuse-cleanup, gamification-cleanup, purge-verification-sessions), each with a plain name, one line saying what it deletes, how often it runs, when it last ran successfully, when it last failed, and its state in words with an icon: "Running as expected", "Late" (last success older than twice its period), "Failing" (failed since its last success) or "No record yet". 🔴 Nothing recorded is "No record yet", never fine, and a record the server cannot read says "Could not be read". The page says that records for most of these jobs start on the day it went live. To give the scheduled commands a record, a new listener (App\Listeners\StampScheduledCommandOutcome, registered in EventServiceProvider so the separate schedule:finish process also has it) stamps the cache when any scheduled artisan command finishes: schedule:<command>:last_ok_at or :last_failed_at, an ISO time kept 400 days. It covers both ways Laravel reports an end: ScheduledTaskFinished / ScheduledTaskFailed for a foreground task, and ScheduledBackgroundTaskFinished for a runInBackground() task (whose launch, with no exit code yet, stamps nothing). A closure task, or a run skipped because the previous one is still going, stamps nothing; a cache failure is logged once per process and never stops the scheduler. The every-minute runner's jobs read cron_logs (kept 30 days), and retention:enforce also reads tenant_retention_runs. backup:verify now also writes its verdict to the cache on every run, healthy or not (backup:verify:status: state, when the newest backup was made, its age and size, when it was checked; kept 3 days); what it checks and when it alarms are unchanged. Two new home page cards: Clean-up jobs (the worst state on the page; "Could not be checked" while nothing is recorded) and Database backup ("Fine" when the last verdict is healthy and under 26 hours old, "Not working" when it says the backup is stale, missing, empty or unreadable, "Could not be checked" with no recent verdict, as on a developer's computer), which also says plainly that a copy kept off the server and the monthly restore test are not recorded anywhere it can read. Endpoint GET /v2/platform-team/clean-up-jobs, platform team only; it sends only the job, how often, the two times, the state and whether the record could be read, never a job's output or error text. Wording in all eleven languages. Tests: ScheduledCommandStampsTest (the framework's own event classes: foreground success and failure, background launch then finish, background failure, an overlap skip, a closure, the real schedule:finish command, a broken cache), CleanUpJobsTest (exact keys; nothing recorded is unknown; stamps, the runner's log and the retention record; an unreadable log; the fixed list matches the schedule and the runner), BackupVerifyTest, PlatformHealthSummaryTest, CleanUpJobsPage.test.tsx, PlatformTeamHome.test.tsx.
  • Data requests: how many requests about members' own data are waiting in every community, and for how long (16 Nov 2026): new page /platform-team/data-requests in the Platform team panel, the first entry under Data and legal. Until now these could only be seen one community at a time, in that community's own admin panel. For every community, including those with nothing open, the page shows how many data requests are open (waiting or being worked on), which kinds they are (a copy of their data, erasure, a correction, a limit on use, a transfer, an objection), how many are overdue (open for more than 30 days), how many are nearly due (open 25 to 30 days), how many days the oldest open one has waited, and how many were completed in the last 90 days, with a total row. The page names the communities that have an overdue request at the top and says the rule in words: overdue means open for more than 30 days, and the clock starts when the request was made. These are the platform's existing rules (the community GDPR dashboard's 30 days and its clock; the daily overdue alarm's 25 days), not new ones. Counts only: no member, no request number, no address, token, export file or note leaves the server. A figure the server cannot read says "Not available", never zero. Requests are still answered in each community's own admin panel; this page changes nothing. Endpoint GET /v2/platform-team/data-requests, platform team only (route middleware and a check in the controller). Wording in all eleven languages.
